synthesis.paragraph: Three of today's papers carry the tag "Urban Green Space and Health," which include a narrative review on the built environment and subjective well-being, a study on children's contact with nature in Beijing, and a multimodal framework for assessing pedestrian well-being. The tag "Urban Transport and Accessibility" also covers three papers, sharing the narrative review on subjective well-being and the multimodal pedestrian framework, alongside a paper applying Daoist philosophy to transport decarbonisation. Outside of these groups, one study fine-tuned pre-trained language models to extract structured information from free-text crash narratives, another simulated semi-on-demand transit services using shared autonomous vehicles in Munich, and a third synthesized agglomeration theory and land value taxation through a literature review and expert interviews.
